expect.value: RESTORED OK - original inverter settings verified

failure_outcome: the Phase-B guard sets the RAM lease from the commit result alone (no read-back); a commit that reports success without storing the marker lets the lease run on RAM only, and after a reboot its override is silent (Dump: 244 = 0 and the ceiling live, unsupervised)
notes: F-PB01-4, DUPLICATE of F-FW06-3 (FW-06 owns it; this is its used-device stale-CLEAR form, as FW-06-c and the suite's [9]), signature false-positive-commit. V0.1 (brief B5): the document starts with a completed Dump lease (the corpus PB-01-b prelude: telemetry, a 1-minute Dump START, run_for 400 s; its verified restore commits the marker CLEAR, FW:20389-20397, status 'RESTORED OK - original inverter settings verified' FW:20419), so dump.valid was stored before the injected false_positive: _lab_fw's NVS USED-KEY RULE refuses a commit fault on a key never stored earlier in the run, so the V0 never-used variant (marker ABSENT, end state equal to F-FW04-1) is no longer injected. Expected marker CLEAR: the false_positive Phase-B commit (FW:18547-18548) stores nothing and returns true (lab primitive), production commit_record only reports the save / sync result (ecco_durable_snapshot.h:93-98) and a commit that stores nothing leaves the stored record untouched (_dump_sim.py:284-286), and markers are never deleted by firmware (S4); the boot reads the stored CLEAR (FW:801-804: dump_snapshot_valid false), no operator flag, so status 'Inactive' (FW:929) while 244 = 0 written by the START stays live. FINDING-NEW: S4 states generically that a commit result can be a false positive (retry-record context); the Phase-B marker case and its consequence are not documented, and PLATFORM-ABSENT (READ_ERROR, then ABSENT) matches neither the trigger nor the used-device boot read. Severity: safety, bounded as F-FW04-1 (Dump: 244 = 0 and the ceiling live, unsupervised, status 'Inactive'); Free Power twin: cost. Reachability: UNKNOWN (trigger MODEL-dependent): S4 states that a commit result can be a false positive, but in ESPHome 2026.8.2 commit_record's save() always queues and sync() returns false when nvs_set_blob errors, so True means the write returned ESP_OK in that call; a physical route needs a silent flash program failure and, for this stale CLEAR, the old entry's erase failing silently too; then a reboot during the lease. MODEL: nvs_policy false_positive (nothing stored, True). Synthetic values only.
ownership: one dongle; Free Power and Dump to Grid leases, register 244 and the manual TOU owner domains as the firmware defines them; the synthetic SITE is the owner's ORIGINAL; an owner change outside any lease is the new ORIGINAL, a change while a domain holds the register is foreign (excluded until ECCO rewrites it)
smallest_safe_repair_scope: only if such a trigger is confirmed: in the three Phase-B guards (FP, Dump, reg244) read the marker back with the existing direct NVS read primitive read_direct_t (not load_record, which can be served from the pending-save queue) before the RAM mirror is set and before any override write; require RESTORE_REQUIRED, else take the existing commit-failure path (START FAILED, nothing written). No write path added. The F-FW04-1 boot cross-check covers only the never-used variant. Description only

source_anchors.text: The commit result itself can be a false negative or a false positive
Returns true only if BOTH the queue step and the flash sync succeeded
Markers are never deleted by firmware

title: A Phase-B Dump marker commit that returns true without storing the record (lab false_positive) on a used device, then a reboot during the lease: the marker keeps the previous lease's CLEAR, the boot reads CLEAR and export stays enabled (244 = 0) with no visible obligation
